title: Azure Monitor Data Flow
summary: From data sources through diagnostic settings and data collection rules into metrics and Log Analytics — and out to alerts, action groups and workbooks.

nodes.label: Azure resources
nodes.detail: Emit platform metrics automatically. Resource logs need a diagnostic setting.

nodes.label: VM guest OS
nodes.detail: AMA collects performance counters, Windows events and syslog based on data collection rules.

nodes.label: Activity log
nodes.detail: Who did what at the subscription level. 90 days in the portal; export with a diagnostic setting.

nodes.label: Applications
nodes.detail: App telemetry (requests, dependencies, exceptions) via Application Insights, stored in a workspace.

nodes.label: Diagnostic settings
nodes.detail: Send resource logs/metrics to Log Analytics, storage (archive) or Event Hubs (stream to SIEM).

nodes.label: Data collection rule
nodes.detail: Defines data sources, transformations and destinations for the agent.

nodes.label: Metrics store
nodes.detail: Lightweight numeric time series for near-real-time charts and alerts.

nodes.label: Log Analytics
nodes.detail: Stores logs in tables; query with KQL; set retention per table/workspace.

nodes.label: Metrics explorer
nodes.detail: Chart metrics with aggregation and splitting; pin to dashboards.

nodes.label: Alert rules
nodes.detail: Evaluate conditions and fire alerts.

nodes.label: Action groups
nodes.detail: Email, SMS, push, voice, webhook, Logic App, Function, runbook, ITSM.

nodes.label: Workbooks
nodes.detail: Interactive reports and curated experiences such as VM insights.

steps.title: Metrics flow automatically
steps.text: Platform metrics land in the metrics store without configuration.

steps.title: Logs need routing
steps.text: Resource logs require a diagnostic setting; guest OS data requires AMA + a DCR.

steps.title: Query
steps.text: Everything in the workspace is queryable with KQL and visualized in workbooks.

steps.title: Alert and act
steps.text: Alert rules evaluate metrics or logs and trigger action groups.

examExpects: Diagnostic settings are required to collect resource logs; pick the destination by purpose (analyze, archive, stream).
AMA + DCRs collect guest OS data; the legacy Log Analytics agent is retired.
Metrics vs logs: numeric/near-real-time vs rich/queryable.
Alert rules + action groups (+ processing rules) form the notification path.

title: Azure Backup & Site Recovery Architecture
summary: What each vault type protects, how policies drive recovery points, restore options — and how Site Recovery differs.

nodes.label: Azure VMs
nodes.detail: VM backups take snapshots (instant restore) then transfer to the vault.

nodes.label: Azure Files
nodes.detail: Azure Files backup is managed by a Recovery Services vault using share snapshots.

nodes.label: On-prem files
nodes.detail: The MARS agent backs up Windows files, folders and system state directly to a Recovery Services vault.

nodes.label: Disks & Blobs
nodes.detail: Managed disks, blobs, PostgreSQL and AKS are protected by a Backup vault.

nodes.label: Backup policy
nodes.detail: Daily/weekly/monthly/yearly retention; enhanced VM policy supports multiple backups per day.

nodes.label: Recovery Services vault
nodes.detail: Set storage redundancy (LRS/ZRS/GRS) before protecting items. Soft delete keeps deleted backups recoverable.

nodes.label: Backup vault
nodes.detail: Protects Azure Disks, Blobs, PostgreSQL, AKS and more.

nodes.label: Restore options
nodes.detail: Create a new VM, restore disks, replace existing disks, or mount a recovery point for file-level recovery.

nodes.label: Cross Region Restore
nodes.detail: With a GRS vault and CRR enabled, restore in the paired region.

nodes.label: Site Recovery replica
nodes.detail: ASR replicates running VMs continuously for failover with low RPO/RTO — a different goal from point-in-time backup.

steps.title: Pick the right vault
steps.text: VMs, Azure Files and MARS go to a Recovery Services vault; disks and blobs to a Backup vault.

steps.title: Policy
steps.text: A backup policy schedules backups and retains recovery points.

steps.title: Restore
steps.text: Restore whole VMs, disks or individual files; with GRS, restore in the secondary region.

steps.title: Site Recovery is different
steps.text: Backup restores data to a point in time; Site Recovery fails over running workloads.

examExpects: Know which vault protects which workload and that VM vaults must be in the VMs' region.
Vault redundancy is fixed once items are protected; GRS enables Cross Region Restore.
File-level restore doesn't require restoring the whole VM.
Backup ≠ disaster recovery: use Site Recovery for low-RTO failover.
